correctness.rationale: The exact finite complex is reconstructed from all 96 forbidden 3-matchings, yielding 3017 augmented faces. A 1504-pair matching has exactly nine critical 3-faces, and exhaustive topological sorting of all 13504 Hasse edges confirms acyclicity. All Morse incidences are integral units. Nine explicit join-of-two-triangle-boundaries sphere cycles are true 3-cycles; their 9x9 integral Morse critical-coordinate matrix is a negative signed permutation with determinant -1, hence a primitive integral homology basis. Every one of 576 product group actions is checked on all nine cycles against exterior-square tensor matrices, and the part swap is the positive tensor flip. An independent signed Lefschetz computation checks 1152 actions. The computation is exhaustive for this finite object, with no infinite extrapolation.

originality.rationale: Theorem 1.4 of Linusson--Shareshian--Welker (2004) establishes only the nine-sphere nonequivariant homotopy type, while its Conjecture 1.14 explicitly asks for the hook-tensor homology representation and does not establish it. The current finite result identifies an integral tensor lattice with primitive cycles and determines the additional part-interchange action. Holmsen--Lee (2020) prove general vanishing and Leray bounds rather than this representation. Searches of published mathematical records and the relevant prior research claims found only results on different graph complexes, with the residual risk of unindexed equivalent work.
residual_risks: An unindexed or unpublished equivalent calculation of BNM_3(4,4) may exist.
The index-only sources were not used to assert the absence of a theorem from their full papers.
Independent specialist verification of the new integer Morse-to-representation argument has not been performed.

value.rationale: The 4-by-4 board at matching threshold three is the smallest balanced instance of the 2004 hook-tensor representation question whose top homology rank is greater than one: rank 9 instead of 1 on 3-by-3. The explicit integral tensor module and positive part-interchange action go beyond the known sphere rank and beyond a rational character check, and give usable primitive cycle generators for a canonical test of a named open representation conjecture. The result is exact and natural although finite; it does not claim to resolve the full conjecture.
